newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian leaders meet on tense Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Russian leaders meet on tense Chechnya.

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin told a top level meeting on Chechnya on Saturday that he intended it to take firm decisions to cement the fragile new peace in the region.
In his opening remarks Chernomyrdin, who is deputising for President Boris Yeltsin as he undergoes clinical checks ahead of heart surgery, said he wanted to take "substantive decisions".

"The main thing now is to determine what to do next and within which framework we should operate, deciding the political and recovery aspects of the Chechen settlement," Itar-Tass news agency quoted Chernomyrdin as telling the meeting.

Alexander Lebed, the Kremlin security chief who signed an ambitious peace with the separatist rebels on August 31, opened his report to the meeting saying: "It is essential to decide with collective wisdom which steps should be taken to settle the Chechen crisis after the signing of the Khasav-Yurt accords."
Lebed signed the deal at Khasav-Yurt, just outside Chechnya, agreeing to withdraw Russian troops and defer for five years a resolution of the separatists' demands for full independence.
Chernomyrdin gave it a cool response, insisting it was a political "statement of intention", not a legally binding peace treaty. He stressed Moscow will never agree to secession.

With Yeltsin sidelined by his forthcoming surgery, Lebed's rivals for power in Moscow have seized on his apparently leaving open the question of independence to criticise the former general, who makes no secret of his presidential ambitions.

Sources close to Chernomyrdin were quoted on Friday as saying the so-called "power ministers", including defence and interior, would attend the meeting, although they were not mentioned in reports on Saturday.

Yeltsin, who has direct control over the power ministries, handed some of those responsibilities on to Chernomyrdin while he undergoes treatment. The 65-year-old president was spending the weekend in a Moscow clinic for more pre-surgical checks.
His influential chief-of-staff, Anatoly Chubais, was at the meeting, Russian news agencies said, as were the chief of the Russian general staff and the justice minister among others.

In Chechnya, a three-way conflict has been brewing between Russian troops, the separatist rebels who seized the capital Grozny last month and the pro-Moscow Chechen administration, which Lebed pointedly left out of his peace settlement.
Tass quoted the Russian interior ministry forces in Grozny as saying there had been no shooting at troops overnight.
But, a spokesman said, an unnamed separatist commander had been shot dead in a dispute with pro-Moscow Chechens in the predominantly loyalist north of the mainly Moslem region.
An army spokesman told Interfax news agency that separatists had shot at a guard post near Grozny's Severny airport and military base, causing no casualties.
He said it was the latest in a series of incidents in which he accused the rebels of trying to "provoke a conflict".
The Russian commander in the region suspended planned troop withdrawals almost as soon as they had begun last week, complaining of disputes over the exchange of prisoners.
Separatist leaders warned this was "senseless brinkmanship" and warned they were "ready for any eventuality", although insisted they would seek a peaceful resolution.
In Grozny, Russian forces and separatist delegates were due to hold more meetings on Saturday to try to settle a variety of complaints on either side.
